chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus ibn Yaqub, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I pray (individually), then I enter the mosque, and the prayer is established, and I have already prayed.' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'Pray with them. Allah will choose the one of the two that is more beloved to Him.'

key_terms.أَحَبَّهُمَا: The more beloved of the two

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I have already prayed individually but enter the mosque during the congregational prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the issue of *Salat al-Fard* (obligatory prayer) performed individually before joining the congregation, ruling that the individual does not need to repeat the prayer but should join the *Jam'at* to gain the communal reward. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the congregational prayer serves as a supererogatory enhancement (*Tatawwu'*) rather than a mandatory repetition of the core obligation, with the divine selection of the 'more beloved' act emphasizing the spiritual merit of unity and following the Imam. The phrase 'Allah chooses what is more beloved to Him' underscores the concept of *Ikhtiyar* (divine preference) in rewarding the intention and context of the worshipper.
